Evan —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a concise commercial approach and a sample amortization table (CSV) that maps committed tranches to quarterly invoice credits. Summary below — will follow up with a short walkthrough link.

1) Contracting options (high-level)
- Conservative: 12-month committed token pool (baseline), flat per-1k-token rate at list minus 8% commit discount; overages billed at list + 25% (no burst credits). Good if you need minimal lock-in.
- Balanced (recommended): 36-month signed commitment with annual tranches (Year1 baseline, Year2 ramp +15%, Year3 optional +10% uplift). Per-1k rate = list minus 18% for committed usage, overages billed at list rate with a 10% graceband first year (applies as invoice credit).
- Aggressive: 36-month higher-commit tier with staged step-down pricing (deeper discounts at higher tranches), includes burst cushion credits and carry-forward credits for underuse.

2) Invoice-hedge mechanism (our standard "credit ladder")
- Mechanic: Customer prepays token credits into a locked ladder (quarterly tranches). Each quarter, the ladder amortizes a proportional invoice credit against committed consumption. If monthly usage spikes above committed monthly profile, the ladder provides a burn-down buffer (prepaid credits applied first) to avoid immediate overage charges.
- Convertibility: Prepaid credits are convertible to streaming calls (same redemption) and to model-variant fallbacks. Unused credits roll forward per contract rules (see expiry below).
- Accounting on invoices: We show: gross usage, prepaid credit applied, net billed usage. Any remaining overage is invoiced at the overage rate.

3) Overages, gracebands, and expiry
- Graceband: By default we propose a 10% rolling graceband in Year1 that can be reduced in subsequent years. The graceband absorbs transient spikes without triggering overage invoices (converted into credit adjustments).
- Netting: Credits and usage are netted at the account (company) level per region. If you require separate BU-level netting, we can add carveouts.
- Expiry: Prepaid credits amortize over 12 months from purchase; unamortized credits beyond contract termination are refundable on a pro-rata basis (or convertible to an extended-use pool at a reduced rate).

4) Operational notes & gating items
- Metering: Token meters are exported per route/model; we provide token-level detail each invoice cycle.
- Auditability: Monthly usage CSV and a monthly reconciliation report (we include a sample in the attached CSV).

Attachments: 2026-11-02-Token-Procurement-Schedule-Table.csv (sample quarterly amortization + scenario columns)

Next steps: I'll schedule a 30-min call for Wed/Thu to walk the procurement and finance teams through the amortization table and how the credits appear on invoices. If you prefer, we can produce a balanced-term redline for legal next.

Best,

Evan —

Looping in a few commercial clarifications and a redlined term-sheet for your procurement review. Key redlines we suggest for the Balanced option:

- Graceband behavior: 10% rolling in Year1, then 5% Year2+, with triggers for sustained overuse (>3 months above threshold) to convert to a permanent uplift.
- Netting/Carveouts: Default netting is account-level; if you want cargo and operations to be separate billed entities we will add carveouts (this affects bucket allocation and discounting).
- Holdback on termination: Standard 60-day wind-down with pro-rata refund on unused prepaid credits after deduction for final consumption.
- Price protection: We can offer annual CPI-based cap on list price increases or lock list price for the first 24 months depending on the commit level.

I've attached the redlined commercial term sheet (commercial-term-sheet-v1-redlines.pdf). A few notes in the PDF: proposed language for rollover credits, an example of convertibility to streaming, and an optional clause to allow one-time redistribution of credits between regions (requires 30 days notice).

Jordan, Rishi — if you can confirm the refundable credit language and the 60-day wind-down text are okay, Evan's team can route this to legal. Evan — happy to take a 20-min call to walk the redlines.

Regards,

Marissa Cole
